questions.question: Which Indian city is known as the 'Pink City'?
questions.rationale: Jaipur's old city was painted pink for the 1876 visit of the Prince of Wales, and a later law kept it pink. Jodhpur is the Blue (and Sun) City — the standing trap.

questions.question: The 'City of Joy' is:
questions.rationale: The nickname comes from Dominique Lapierre's 1985 novel set in Kolkata's slums. Varanasi tempts candidates with its spiritual aura, but the book title decides it.

questions.question: Which city is called the 'Manchester of India'?
questions.rationale: Ahmedabad's textile mills earned it the title in the 19th-20th century. Coimbatore holds the 'Manchester of South India' variant.

questions.question: The 'Silicon Valley of India' refers to:
questions.rationale: Bengaluru's IT industry earned the label. Hyderabad's parallel claim is 'Cyberabad' — the examiner's favourite alternative option.

questions.question: Which city is known as the 'Detroit of India'?
questions.rationale: Chennai's automobile manufacturing cluster earned the American motor-city comparison. Jamshedpur's equivalent is the 'Pittsburgh of India' (steel).

questions.question: The 'Queen of the Arabian Sea' is:
questions.rationale: Kochi's historic spice-trade harbour carries the title. Mumbai's nickname set runs differently — 'City of Dreams' and the financial capital.

questions.question: Which city is famous as the 'Steel City of India'?
questions.rationale: Jamshedpur grew around Tata Steel's 1907 plant — India's first steel city, also called the Pittsburgh of India. Bhilai is the usual decoy.

questions.question: The 'Venice of the East' among Kerala's cities is:
questions.rationale: Alappuzha's backwater canals and houseboats hold the Kerala claim; Udaipur carries the title in Rajasthan. Answer by region when both appear.

questions.question: Which city is known as the 'Diamond City' of India?
questions.rationale: Surat cuts and polishes the overwhelming majority of the world's diamonds, giving it the title.

questions.question: The 'Oxford of the East' is usually identified with:
questions.rationale: Pune's dense cluster of universities and colleges earned the comparison. Madurai, for its ancient Tamil tradition, is the 'Athens of the East'.
